paragraphs: Rabbi Elazar ben Hakkappar. (a) Kol Hatzelamim 43a; Avot, chapter 4: Elazar Hakkappar. I think Hakkappar should be read. (A place name, where he and his son bar Kappara are buried, Gelilot Eretz Yisrael. I do not understand why his son would be bar Kappara.) Jerusalem Talmud, Beitzah, chapter 1, halakhah 3: one of four unanswered matters of Chiyya, answered by Elazar, son of Elazar Hakkappar. Babylonian Chullin 84b instead: Elazar Hakkappar Berabbi answered, “If circumcision,” etc. Likewise Tosefta, Beitzah, chapter 1 [the checked Tosefta brackets “son of”] (see Abba Arikha), and Chullin, chapter 6. Elazar Hakkappar says, “Great is peace,” etc. Elazar son of Elazar Hakkappar says, “Great is peace,” etc., Sifrei Naso, “May the Lord lift His face”; Heilprin says Yalkut Naso omits “Elazar son of” [the checked edition brackets the patronymic]. Tosefta, Ketubbot, chapter 5: Menachem ben Nappach from Hakkappar tells how Tarfon betrothed three hundred women to feed them terumah in famine. Ellu Tereifot 56b: Yehoshua ben Levi sent a hen before Hakkappar Berabbi. Avodah Zarah 43: “I once followed Hakkappar Berabbi.” Ta'anit 11a: Hakkappar Berabbi; Rashi explains Berabbi as an honorific for a distinguished man [the gloss appears on 43a]; see Berabbi. Nazir 19a, “For sinning against the soul”: Hakkappar Berabbi said; Nedarim 10a; Bava Kamma 91b.

(b) In the Shabbat chapter on circumcision, he appears alongside Shimon ben Elazar. Kissui Haddam 84b apparently places Hakkappar with Chiyya. True, but the Jerusalem Talmud and Tosefta parallel has his son answering, as shown; likely Chullin should too, since Sifrei also cites the son. Apparently late, though Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer includes him: later authors made its chapters, or there were two. Matya ben Charash, Eliezer the great’s student, visited Yishmael ben Elazar Hakkappar, Avot de-Rabbi Natan 29, asking about four divisions of atonement. In Mekhilta, Yitro, Bachodesh Hasshelishi, section 7, Matya visits Elazar Hakkappar [the checked text reads simply “Rabbi Elazar”]: “My teacher, have you heard the four divisions?” Either way Hakkappar lived in Eliezer the great’s time. I wished to resolve: father then, son Elazar with Chiyya and Yehoshua ben Levi; read “sent before Eliezer son of Elazar Hakkappar.” But the ancients ascribe Sifrei to Yishmael, and it mentions both father and son, long before Chiyya and Yehoshua ben Levi. Tosefta, Oholot, chapter 18: Rabbi, Yishmael son of Yose, and Hakkappar lodged in a gentile’s shop in Lod, Pinchas ben Yair before them. Necessarily there were two Hakkappars. Rav Huna bar Berekhiah in his name; Chanina bar Chama, his colleague; Nachum bar Pappa in his name.
